title: Consistency-first KV-trim strategies and eviction correctness proof
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As continuous batching increases request concurrency and KV cache density on GPUs, we observe subtle correctness and performance trade-offs when evicting entries. Existing LRU/TTL heuristics can break prefix consistency guarantees under concurrent reads, speculative cache warmups, and multi-model sharing on a single GPU.

Goal: Define a set of KV-trim (eviction) strategies that prioritize correctness (prefix and sequence consistency) while offering tunable cost/latency trade-offs, provide formal invariants and an operational proof sketch, and land a guarded implementation with end-to-end tests and monitoring.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented eviction strategy (or small family of strategies) that ensures: prefix monotonicity (no stale prefix served), causal KV visibility within a request, and safe cross-tenant sharing bounds.
- Implementation gated by a feature flag and runtime config knobs (policy: LRU / TTL / prefix-aware / hybrid, safety-mode: strict/relaxed).
- End-to-end test suite that reproduces previously observed races and asserts invariants under stress.
- Benchmarks showing P99 generation latency regression <= 7% in strict safety-mode for representative workloads vs baseline (no eviction).
- Observable signals (dashboard + SLO) and automated rollback on safety invariant breach.

Proposed design summary:
1) Policy primitives:
   - LRU: recency-based trimming at block granularity, cheap but can evict prefixes used by in-flight requests.
   - TTL: time-based expiration per prefix; avoids evicting freshly used prefixes but needs tuned TTL values per workload.
   - Prefix-aware trimming: treat prefix-keygroups as pin-able ranges; allow atomic pin/unpin around request lifecycles.
   - Hybrid: TTL with LRU fallback and a lightweight pinning for active requests.

2) Correctness invariants (informal):
   - I1 (Prefix Monotonicity): Once a prefix P is observed by an in-flight decoding request, subsequent incremental decodes that depend on P must not see a different (older or incompatible) KV state for P.
   - I2 (KV Atomicity for Request): KV reads performed for a single logical request must reference a consistent snapshot (same generation id) for all keys touched.
   - I3 (Bounded Sharing): For shared-GPU pools, evictions must not cause unresolved cross-tenant contamination (no accidental reuse of stale cache entries across model variants).

3) Runtime mechanisms to satisfy invariants:
   - Pin-by-request: on request start, pin relevant prefix ranges (lightweight refcount) in GPU-resident metadata; pins prevent eviction until request completion or soft timeout.
   - Generation tagging: each KV write/insert increments a small generation counter for the prefix; request reads record the generation and the runtime ensures no mix of older/newer within the same request.
   - Eviction fencing: eviction scans respect current pin refcounts and generation fences; eviction may preemptively mark entries for async GC instead of immediate reclamation when pins exist.

4) Memory optimizations:
   - Block coalescing: align eviction units to contiguous KV blocks to reduce kernel launch overhead and fragmentation.
   - Opportunistic compression on cold entries before eviction to extend working set.
   - Adaptive trimming thresholds based on observed sequence length distributions and batch sizes (runtime ML signal).

Testing and verification plan:
- Unit tests for pin/refcount operations and generation monotonicity.
- Chaos tests: synthetic workload that issues overlapping prefixes with interleaved short/long requests to reproduce race conditions; assert invariants I1/I2.
- Fuzzing: randomized eviction ordering under different policies to find correctness edge-cases.
- Benchmarks: real workloads derived from prod traces (chat short-turns, long context streams) to measure perf and memory usage.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Implement feature-flagged prefix-aware trimming with strict safety-mode on a canary Dedicated pool.
- Stage 2: Run chaos tests and compare invariant metrics; if stable, promote to more pools and enable hybrid policy for perf-benefit testing.
- Stage 3: Default policy becomes hybrid for P95 workloads; strict safety remains opt-in for high-consistency customers.

Observability and alerts:
- New metrics: pin hits/misses, eviction-deferred-count, generation-mismatches-per-request, async-gc-latency.
- Dashboards: per-model and per-pool breakdowns, top offending prefixes.
- Alert: generation-mismatch rate > 0.01% for 5m => automatic rollback and paging to oncall.

Dependencies and risks:
- Requires lightweight atomic pin counter in GPU metadata (runtime change, potential perf tax).
- Async-GC complexity may temporarily increase memory high-water events.
- Incorrect TTL tuning could either waste memory or cause higher miss rates.

Notes: this ticket focuses on correctness-first strategy and proof-of-safety; performance tuning (adaptive thresholds, compression heuristics) will be follow-ups.

2026-03-07 - Design review (Ravi Singh): Recommend adding soft timeouts to pins to avoid permanent leakage from stalled requests; flagged UX for tooling to surface long-pinned prefixes.
2026-03-09 - Security (Lena Ortiz): No customer data is retained beyond existing cache semantics; asked to document KMS/HSM interactions for Private deployments (added to docs draft).

2026-03-11 - Marco Nguyen: Added generation-fence checks and unit tests. Found race where async-GC could clash with pin unclearing; added eviction fencing to avoid immediate reclamation when pin refcount>0.
